summary: A privately owned, glass-walled 30-foot fire-lookout-style rental tower near Wallace, Idaho, built new rather than restored, with a Full Moon and a Half Moon tower.

facts.design: 30-foot tower with a one-room glass-walled cab, a wood stove and a skylight; built to resemble traditional fire lookouts

access.note: Private property managed by the owner; guests reach the towers by booking a stay. The 55 acres are surrounded by Forest Service land.

visit.trail_note: Two forest trails and a swimming hole on the property. In winter the Forest Service closes the road when big snow arrives; a snow-vehicle shuttle is offered for an extra fee.

corrections.why: The listing names this tower Full Moon, and MoonPass Lookouts is the property. Moon Pass is also a county road. Sources describe a new build modeled on traditional lookouts, not a copy of a named historic tower. Human review needed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: TIME (March 2026) counts two newly built towers with three more planned; Seattle Met (September 2026) counts three standing with two more to come; the owner's overview says five. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one number.
The owner's site and the Airbnb listing describe a dry-flush toilet and sauna at ground level; TIME describes a bathroom and sauna in a separate cabin. The story reports both.

sources.title: The Appeal of Sleeping in a Fire Lookout

notes_for_editor: No historic lookout named Moon Pass was found in two searches and the page reads; the towers are new builds, so 'replica' in the record means 'modeled on traditional lookouts', which Seattle Met supports, but no source names a historic tower that was copied. Consider the proposed name correction. Sources are promotional (owner site, Airbnb, Lodgify) for amenities and dimensions, and press (TIME, Seattle Met) for history; no independent or official source describes the property. Tower count differs by source. The record covers Full Moon; Half Moon is a separate Airbnb listing that was not fetched, so it is mentioned only from the FFLA list. The record's access 'permission' is kept. The build year is unknown: TIME says 'newly built' as of March 2026, so no events are listed. Seven sources; reads used: Airbnb, MoonPass site, TIME, Seattle Met (twice), Wallace road page, Lodgify, plus cached FFLA list. Two searches.
